_description: Deterministic redirect rules. A ticket matching a rule is REASSIGNED to another team instead of being remediated here — the recommendation becomes 'route this elsewhere'. Evaluated in order; the first match wins. Read fresh on every call (backend/routing_store.py), so rules can be edited without restarting.
_matching: Each `match_any` entry is a regex, matched case-insensitively against the ticket's searchable text (short_description, description, subcategory, category, work notes, and every labelled field value). `exclude_any` vetoes a match. Regexes — not plain substrings — so word boundaries can be enforced.
_important: Set `assignment_group` to the EXACT ServiceNow assignment-group name for the receiving team. This is not cosmetic: on approval the app PATCHes assignment_group to this exact string, and ServiceNow will reject a name it cannot resolve to a real group.
_reassignment: A rule with an assignment_group makes approval MOVE the ticket to that group (assignment_group only — never state, close, or resolve). Clear the assignment_group to downgrade a rule back to recommend-and-comment.

rules._instructions_note: Supplementary steps only. The engine always emits 'Reassign incident <n> to <group>' as step 1, so do not repeat it here.
instructions: Leave the customer-facing details and any referenced BAN/TN untouched — the receiving team needs them as reported.
Do not close or resolve; ownership transfers and the incident stays open.

_add_more: Add further rules in the same shape, e.g. a TSC rule matching 'fallout to tsc' -> assignment_group 'TSC-Technician Support Center'. Order matters: put the most specific rule first.
